# Image

Header: `winui/ui/media/Image.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/Image.hpp`.

Shows an [ImageSource](../rendering/image-source.md) (a still picture, an animated GIF or an SVG document) stretched into the space layout gives it.

The declarative spec is [`ui::Image`](#uiimage), and the pixels themselves are a [`ui::Bitmap`](../rendering/bitmap.md). Sizing follows the [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) mode, Uniform by default. A nine-grid can keep the corners unscaled. An animated source plays by itself when its `auto_play` is set, and [play()](#play) and [stop()](#stop) control it. It pauses while it is off screen (scrolled out of view, clipped away or not drawn) and goes on from the frame it showed when it comes back. The image takes no input.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
window.set_content(ui::Image{
    .source  = ui::Bitmap::read_png("photo.png"),
    .stretch = ui::Stretch::UniformToFill,
    .width   = 320.0f,
    .height  = 200.0f,
});

// Imperative, an animated GIF:
auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* gif   = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ImageControl>(ui::AnimatedImage::read("spinner.gif")));
gif->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::None);
auto* pause = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Pause"));
pause->on_click([gif] { gif->is_playing() ? gif->stop() : gif->play(); });
```

## `ui::Image`

An image: a still picture, an animated GIF or an SVG document, stretched into its space. Builds a [ui::ImageControl](#uiimagecontrol). The pixels themselves are a [`ui::Bitmap`](../rendering/bitmap.md).

[`source`](#uiimage-source) takes any of the three, since [ui::ImageSource](../rendering/image-source.md) converts from each. It can be bound. A [Binding](../core/binding.md) doesn't compare its values, only the [Property](../core/property.md) behind it does, so `bind(choice, [](int i) -> ui::ImageSource { ... })` swaps pictures as `choice` changes.

Example: 
```cpp
std::vector<ui::Bitmap> photos = {ui::Bitmap::read("cliff.jpg"), ui::Bitmap::read("lake.jpg")};
ui::Property<int> choice{0};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
    ui::Image{.source  = ui::bind(choice, [&photos](int i) -> ui::ImageSource { return photos[i]; }),
              .stretch = ui::Stretch::UniformToFill,
              .width   = 300.0f,
              .height  = 200.0f},
    ui::Button{.text = "Next", .on_click = [&] { choice = (choice.get() + 1) % 2; }},
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Image{
    .source, .stretch, .nine_grid, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_image_opened, .on_image_failed, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uiimage-source"></span>`source` | `ui::Binding<ui::ImageSource>` |  | The picture: a bitmap, an animated image or an SVG document. Empty draws nothing. |
| <span id="uiimage-stretch"></span>`stretch` | `ui::Binding<ui::Stretch>` | `{ui::Stretch::Uniform}` | How the picture fills the element's box. Uniform, the default, keeps the aspect ratio. |
| <span id="uiimage-nine_grid"></span>`nine_grid` | `ui::Binding<ui::Thickness>` |  | The nine-grid insets, in the picture's pixels. The corners keep their size and the edges and center stretch. Zero, the default, draws the picture whole. |
| <span id="uiimage-on_image_opened"></span>`on_image_opened` | `ui::Callback<void()>` |  | A source made by [ImageSource::load()](../rendering/image-source.md#load) finished decoding ([ImageControl::on_image_opened()](#on_image_opened)). |
| <span id="uiimage-on_image_failed"></span>`on_image_failed` | `ui::Callback<void(std::string_view)>` |  | A source made by [ImageSource::load()](../rendering/image-source.md#load) failed, with the reason ([ImageControl::on_image_failed()](#on_image_failed)). |
| <span id="uiimage-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uiimage-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uiimage-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uiimage-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uiimage-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uiimage-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uiimage-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Image>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

## `ui::ImageControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

Shows an [ImageSource](../rendering/image-source.md) (a still picture, an animated GIF or an SVG document) stretched into the space layout gives it.

The declarative spec is [`ui::Image`](#uiimage), and the pixels themselves are a [`ui::Bitmap`](../rendering/bitmap.md). Sizing follows the [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) mode, Uniform by default. A nine-grid can keep the corners unscaled. An animated source plays by itself when its `auto_play` is set, and [play()](#play) and [stop()](#stop) control it. It pauses while it is off screen (scrolled out of view, clipped away or not drawn) and goes on from the frame it showed when it comes back. The image takes no input.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative:
window.set_content(ui::Image{
    .source  = ui::Bitmap::read_png("photo.png"),
    .stretch = ui::Stretch::UniformToFill,
    .width   = 320.0f,
    .height  = 200.0f,
});

// Imperative, an animated GIF:
auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* gif   = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ImageControl>(ui::AnimatedImage::read("spinner.gif")));
gif->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::None);
auto* pause = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Pause"));
pause->on_click([gif] { gif->is_playing() ? gif->stop() : gif->play(); });
```

### ImageControl

```cpp
ImageControl() = default
```

An empty image. It measures to zero and draws nothing.

### ImageControl

```cpp
ImageControl(ImageSource source)
```

An image showing [`source`](#source). An animated source with `auto_play` set starts playing.

### source

```cpp
const ImageSource& source() const
```

The picture shown.

### set_source

```cpp
void set_source(ImageSource source)
```

Replaces the picture and updates layout. Starts an animated source playing when its `auto_play` says so. A source still loading through [ImageSource::load()](../rendering/image-source.md#load) draws nothing until its decode is done. Then the control updates its layout and raises [on_image_opened()](#on_image_opened) or [on_image_failed()](#on_image_failed). The window stays idle while the picture decodes.

### on_image_opened

```cpp
void on_image_opened(Callback<void()> handler)
```

Fires when a source made by [ImageSource::load()](../rendering/image-source.md#load) has finished decoding and shows.

### on_image_failed

```cpp
void on_image_failed(Callback<void(std::string_view)> handler)
```

Fires when a source made by [ImageSource::load()](../rendering/image-source.md#load) could not be read or decoded. The handler gets the reason.

### stretch

```cpp
Stretch stretch() const
```

How the picture fills the element's box. Uniform by default.

```cpp
void set_stretch(Stretch stretch)
```

Sets the stretch mode. Updates layout and redraws.

```cpp

```

The nine-grid insets, in the picture's pixels. Zero, the default, draws the picture whole. Ignored for an SVG source.


Sets the nine-grid insets. Redraws.

### is_animated

```cpp
bool is_animated() const
```

Whether the source has more than one frame.

### is_playing

```cpp
bool is_playing() const
```

Whether the animation plays. [play()](#play) sets it and [stop()](#stop) clears it. An animation that ran to its end still reports true.

### play

```cpp
void play()
```

Restarts a stopped animation. Does nothing to one already running or one that ran to its end.

### stop

```cpp
void stop()
```

Stops and rewinds to the first frame.

### current_frame

```cpp
std::size_t current_frame() const
```

The index of the frame showing, 0 for a still source.

### parallel_measure_safe

```cpp
bool parallel_measure_safe() const override
```

Returns true, since measuring reads only the source's size.

### on_screen_changed

```cpp
void on_screen_changed(bool on_screen) override
```

Called after a frame in which [on_screen()](../tree/element.md#on_screen) changed, for an element that called [set_screen_tracking()](../tree/element.md#set_screen_tracking). The frame that brings an element back into view calls it with true, so a control that paused its clock off screen restarts it here ([request_tick_in()](../tree/element.md#request_tick_in) works from it). The default does nothing.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

What screen readers and other assistive tools see of this node: the role, name, help text and children here, and what a client can do with the node through the providers [automation_providers()](../tree/element.md#automation_providers) lists (ui/Automation.hpp).

[automation_role()](#automation_role) is the role this node reports; Group by default.

### placement

```cpp
Placement placement() const
```

Computes the [Placement](#struct-placement) for the current bounds and source.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](../tree/element.md#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

This element's own part of [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick): a clock of its own ([ToolTip](tool-tip.md#uitooltip)'s hover delay, an animation's phase, a caret blink). Runs after the visual layer has advanced and before the children are ticked, which [tick()](../tree/element.md#tick) does by itself. Tick only parts that [for_each_child()](../tree/element.md#for_each_child) does not list here. Default: nothing.

### struct Placement

Where the picture lands and which part of it shows, for the current bounds.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Rect` |  | The whole picture's rect, in DIPs. It may extend past the element. |
| `visible` | `Rect` |  | The part of the element's drawing that isn't clipped away. |
